questions.question: What evidence supports this claim: "7-day-ahead global fire forecast error is significantly below the operational persistence forecast" (paper arXiv:2610.11022)?
questions.gold_text: 0.1deg MSE: 2023 lead-1 -32%, lead-7 -43%; 2024 -24% and -40% vs persistence

questions.question: What is the counterexample or limit for this claim: "7-day-ahead global fire forecast error is significantly below the operational persistence forecast" (paper arXiv:2610.11022)?
questions.gold_text: The advantage grows with lead time because the 'no-change' assumption degrades faster - it does not mean high absolute 7-day accuracy

What evidence supports this claim: "Operational fire-source data is severely stale" (paper arXiv:2610.11022)?
questions.gold_text: Satellite fire product has ~1.5 day latency and is then frozen unchanged through the following 5 days of operational forecasts (7 days frozen in the experimental version)

questions.question: What is the counterexample or limit for this claim: "Operational fire-source data is severely stale" (paper arXiv:2610.11022)?
questions.gold_text: Scope limit (not a counter-result): the staleness described covers one operational chain only - NOAA GEFS-Aerosols initialised from GBBEPx; fire inputs at other centres are outside this claim's coverage

questions.question: What is the counterexample or limit for this claim: "Large-fire locations are reliable" (paper arXiv:2610.11022)?
questions.gold_text: Large-fire radiative power is systematically underestimated; small-fire locations are often wrong - intensity calibration and small-fire localisation are the authors' own two 'lessons before deployment'

questions.gold_text: Retrained in 10 regions on six continents: wins all 60 region-lead comparisons vs persistence, 57 vs same-scale learning models; energy score 4.9% below same-input rivals, 11%-65% below statistical baselines

questions.question: What method was used in the paper arXiv:2610.11022 ("A Graph Neural Network for Global Daily Fire Radiative Power Prediction at Medium-Range Lead Times")?
questions.gold_text: Spatiotemporal GNN (grid cells linked by geographic proximity); inputs: historical fire points + reanalysis meteorology + land cover/vegetation; trained 2020-2022, fully held-out test 2023 and 2024; baseline: operational persistence forecast.

questions.question: What method was used in the paper arXiv:2610.09898 ("Learning joint probabilistic weather forecasts from station observations alone (CLARA)")?
questions.gold_text: Wind-direction-biased attention (upwind positions back-tracked by lead time, weights decay with lead) + five-variable joint Gaussian output; station observations only, no NWP or reanalysis inputs.

questions.question: What method was used in the paper arXiv:2610.07583; code: github.com/AikyamLab/climate_xai ("Mechanistic Interpretability of Atmospheric Rivers in GraphCast")?
questions.gold_text: Sparse autoencoders (Matryoshka variant) fitted at GraphCast processor layers 0/8/15 as a 'concept dictionary' (512-dim activations -> 4096 entries); concepts matched against real atmospheric phenomena, with internal activation interventions to test causality.
